primary_claim: MUDMAN, which combines a selective update rule (Disruption Masking) with MAML-based meta-learning, outperforms the current state-of-the-art unlearning method TAR by 40% in robustness to fine-tuning attacks.
stated_future_work: We're sure there are much more low-hanging selectivity improvements to be picked. Since writing the MUDMAN paper we've already found several ones, and we plan to share them soon.
Aim to completely eradicate unwanted tendencies (e.g. deceptiveness, power-seeking, sycophancy) before starting RL
Investigate whether tendencies still creep in during RL in subtle ways
limitations_stated: Tendencies are harder to separate from general capabilities than facts, so unlearning them may be trickier
